Perform multiple-testing adjustment using Efron's empirical null

Source: R/multtest.R
multtest.Rd

Estimates the empirical null distribution \(N(\mu_0, \sigma_0^2)\) of the Gaussianized test statistics and converts every statistic to a two-sided p-value under it, followed by a Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment.

Usage

multtest(teststat_vec, observed_quantile = c(0.05, 0.95))

Arguments

teststat_vec

Named vector of finite Gaussian-like test statistics, one per gene.

observed_quantile

Two numbers in (0, 1), the lower and upper quantiles of teststat_vec that delimit the central subset used by the two fallback estimators.

Value

A list with fdr_vec (BH-adjusted p-values), logpvalue_vec (\(-\log_{10}\) of the two-sided p-values), method (which estimator produced the null), null_mean, null_sd, and pvalue_vec (the two-sided p-values). All vectors carry names(teststat_vec).

Details

Three estimators of the null are tried in order, each only when the previous one fails: locfdr::locfdr (method = "locfdr"), the truncated-Gaussian maximum-likelihood estimator of Efron (2007, Equation 4.12) fitted to the statistics between the two observed_quantile quantiles (method = "truncated_mle"), and a moment-matching estimator on the same central subset (method = "simple"). A warning is raised whenever the chain falls below locfdr, so a degraded null is never silent; the estimator that ran is returned as method.

Examples

set.seed(10)
# 300 null statistics from N(0.2, 1.1^2) plus a few real signals
teststat_vec <- c(stats::rnorm(300, mean = 0.2, sd = 1.1), 6, -7, 8)
names(teststat_vec) <- paste0("gene", seq_along(teststat_vec))
res <- multtest(teststat_vec)
res$method
#> [1] "locfdr"
c(res$null_mean, res$null_sd)
#> [1] 0.1050933 1.0976984
which(res$fdr_vec < 0.05)
#> gene301 gene302 gene303 
#>     301     302     303
